title: Terminal m is a bound boundary realization only when source-member opposition is licensed
summary: GDT800 finds broad stem-conditioned l/m terminal asymmetry but only one circular same-member l/m pair. A speculative hypothesis is that terminal m is a boundary realization selected by a licensed source-member opposition, not a portable suffix or universal allograph.

design.unit: paired complete stem with independently observed source-member opposition and terminal l/m form
design.contrast: terminal m is an operation selected by source-member status versus m is a portable suffix/allograph independent of source member
design.prediction: Within held source-member pairs, m should occur only when the predeclared opposition is present and should not transfer to unmatched stems; l/m rates among unmatched stems should not predict the source-member distinction.
design.countermodel: The source-member opposition may be an editorial label and terminal m may be a line-final realization unrelated to semantic status.
design.falsifier: Matched source-member pairs show no terminal distinction while unmatched stems reproduce the same m effect, or m transfers across source-member classes without boundary change.
design.principal_risk: GDT800 explicitly withholds lexical, suffix, and semantic interpretation; source-member labels and terminal roles require independent binding.
design.related: Near GDT800/GDT801, but targets a conditional source-member operation rather than the already-tested broad terminal-position effect.

source_evidence.quote:
## What the ending now means—and does not mean

The selected renderer tag is **BOUNDARY_FAVOURED_TERMINAL_SURFACE**, displayed
as “zeilenrandbevorzugte Endform; Wert offen”. This is a structural field, not
a word translation. It improves the architecture from indivisible wholes to
**learned stem/whole plus bound terminal realization**.

The evidence does not license `m=l`, an obligatory final allograph, a case
ending, abbreviation, sound or semantic suffix. There are
**203** paired nonfinal `m` events
and **310** paired final `l` events. Both A09 labels are
standalone units, so the running-text edge model cannot predict why f70 takes
B2 and f72 B3. That direction remains a local whole-label/status rival.
